title: Service reliability change sprint templates and guardrails (Oct 2026)
content:
Purpose / TL;DR:
This is a working playbook for running short (1–3 sprint) cross-functional reliability change efforts that touch SLOs, alerting, and routing. The goal: give feature teams and platform partners a light-weight, repeatable sprint template and a set of operational guardrails so we land changes with predictable risk and clear rollback/fallback paths.

Audience:
- Feature teams making behavior or traffic-shaping changes that will impact customer-facing SLOs
- Platform teams (serving-runtime, platform-engineering) shipping infra changes
- Eng-SRE and oncall owners who need to approve and run the cutover

Context / Why now:
- We keep seeing rollout incidents where model rollouts + batching config change increases tail latency for a subset of customers.
- Need a shorter, prescriptive process than full release playbooks for low/medium risk reliability changes.
- This is intentionally lightweight: 1–3 sprint scope, explicit SLO signal checks, canary plan, and emergency rollback path.

When to use this template:
- Any change that touches request routing, batching/caching, model variants, serving runtime kernel choices, or autoscaler config.
- Changes that could affect 95th/99th latency, error rate, or availability SLOs.
- Not for pure UI copy updates or tiny config tweaks that are pre-approved by SRE via the fast-track (see fast-track checklist below).

Quick summary of steps (one-liner):
1) Pre-sprint: impact assessment + SLI mapping + stakeholder kickoff
2) Sprint 0: experiment/canary plan and guardrail sign-off + test harnesses
3) Implementation sprint(s): instrument, roll out canary, monitor SLO signals, iterate
4) Cutover sprint: controlled ramp, automation hooks, final SLO check
5) Postmortem + quality gating for follow-on rollouts

Sprint templates (pick one depending on complexity):
- Fast (1 week): small config + no infra changes. Owner: feature eng + SRE reviewer.
  * Day 0: Preflight doc + SLI mapping + fast-track checklist
  * Day 1–3: Implementation + unit/integration tests in staging
  * Day 4: 2% canary rollout (1 AZ), 4 hours of elevated monitoring
  * Day 5: If green, 25% ramp. If still green after 8 hours, full rollout.
  * Retro: 30-min async summary, signoff to close.
- Standard (2 sprints / 4 weeks): code + infra + routing change
  * Sprint 0 (week 1): Impact assessment, stakeholder kickoff (product, eng, SRE, infra, solutions eng), define SLIs impacted and acceptance criteria, create canary plan + cutoff thresholds and rollback conditions. Also spin up local load gen and synthetic tests for target SLO windows.
  * Sprint 1 (week 2): Implementation + staging validation + automated SLO smoke tests. Integrate tracing hooks and synthetic test suites into CI.
  * Sprint 2 (week 3–4): Canary rollouts across traffic slices; scheduled watch windows with oncall; gradual ramp according to policy matrix below.
  * Cutover week choreography: final 24–72h watch and contingency.
- Complex (3+ sprints): cross-regional or core runtime changes; propose a multi-phase rollout and engage incident-review board early.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Change Owner (usually feature lead): coordinates the plan, creates the preflight doc, owns the Jira ticket and PRs.
- SRE Reviewer (eng-sre): approves SLI mapping, defines watch windows, sets escalation rules.
- Platform Eng / Serving Runtime: ensures canary infra and fallback paths are possible; prepares runtime knobs.
- Product / PM: signs off on customer impacts and rollback policy.
- Solutions Eng / Customer Success: notifies top impacted customers if rollout touches dedicated/dedicated-like customers.

Preflight checklist (must be completed before canary):
- [ ] SLI mapping doc attached to ticket (latency/error/availability) with baseline numbers and acceptable delta
- [ ] Acceptance criteria: numeric thresholds for 95/99 latency and error rate plus measurement windows
- [ ] Load tests in staging replicating production P95/P99, attach logs/traces
- [ ] Canary target and ramp plan documented (slices by region/customer tier/route)
- [ ] Rollback plan and automated rollback mechanism available (feature-flag or routing flip)
- [ ] Notification plan and pager roster for watch windows
- [ ] Post rollout monitoring dashboard prebuilt and shared (link to dashboard)
- [ ] Risk classification (low/med/high) and SRE approval signature line

Guardrails (operational):
- Do not exceed X% of customer traffic during canary without SRE explicit signoff (default X = 25%).
- Automatic rollback triggers: sustained 2x increase in 99th latency for >30 minutes, or >0.5% absolute increase in global error rate sustained for 15 minutes.
- All canaries require at least one synthetic job covering the target path running every 5 minutes during watch.
- Feature flags should support instant off path routing; if not available, schedule rollback window shorter and increase watch cadence.

SLO / SLI mapping guidance (practical):
- Primary SLOs to check: request success rate (per-route), 95th latency, 99th latency, capacity saturation metrics (GPU queue length), and model correctness regression (if applicable).
- Keep SLO checks lightweight: pre-aggregated metrics for last 5m and 1h windows with comparisons to baseline.
- Define customer-impact slices: free-tier, paid-tier, enterprise-dedicated, region-eu, region-us-west. Track SLO deltas per slice.

Canary decision matrix (example numbers — teams should customize):
- Green: no SLO delta >5% P95 or P99 within the 4-hour watch -> proceed to 25%
- Caution: any SLO delta between 5–15% -> hold and run extended tests + SRE triage
- Rollback: SLO delta >15% or error increases >0.5% -> immediate rollback and hotfix plan

Operational runbook snippets (to copy into the incident runbook):
- Start watch: SRE oncall posts start message in #ops-watch channel, pins dashboard and sampling links.
- Sampling checks: grab 5 traces from p99 tail every 30 minutes during canary; document common failure modes.
- Escalation: if thresholds breached, contact owner -> SRE -> platform lead -> PM, in that order.

Communication plan (internal and customer):
- Internal: pin a single collaboration thread (Slack) and a ticket with the preflight doc; use watch-mode emoji reactions to indicate signal status.
- Customer-facing: Solutions eng to notify enterprise customers 24h prior if they’re in canary slice; include rollback windows and expected observations.

Acceptance criteria for moving from canary -> wider rollout:
- All primary SLOs within acceptable delta for 4–8h post ramp step.
- No regressions found in synthetic correctness tests.
- No increase in p99 error-tail causes that can’t be explained by data distribution shift.

Fast-track checklist (for trivial changes):
- Low-risk classification by SRE and owner
- No infra/runtime changes
- Small config with automated unit tests and staging smoke tests
- No customer slices impacted beyond internal traffic
- If all true, SRE signs off via comment on the ticket and change can go through the fast path.

Examples / templates to paste into Jira ticket (short):
- SLI mapping: 
  * success_rate: url:/v1/generate, window:5m, baseline:99.1%, alert_threshold:98.6%
  * p95_latency_ms: url:/v1/generate, baseline:120ms, threshold:180ms
  * p99_latency_ms: baseline:400ms, threshold:700ms
- Canary slices: 1) 2% internal-only, 2) 5% paid-users-us-west, 3) 25% paid-all-regions

Risk log (keep updated during sprint):
- Known hypothesis: new batching change may increase KV cache misses for long-tail user sequences -> risk: increased p99. Mitigation: add additional KV warm-up step in runtime and add synthetic long sequence test.
- Known unknown: potential interaction with downstream proxy rate-limiter under high concurrency. Action: coordinate with infra team to run concurrency soak test.

Metrics and dashboards to prepare (links to be put in ticket):
- P50/P95/P99 latency per route and per slice
- Error rate per route and per slice
- Request volume and traffic split per slice
- GPU queue length / utilization / tail latency metrics
- Synthetic correctness pass rate and trace sampling dashboard

Postmortem / retro template (short):
- What changed?
- What signals did we have? (metrics, errors, traces, customer reports)
- What went well?
- What surprised us?
- Action items (owner, due date)
- Follow-up: add new synthetic tests? adjust SLO thresholds? change canary policy?

Open questions / discussion items (for SRE sync):
- Should we standardize automatic rollback thresholds across teams or let team-level overrides? Pros/cons noted.
- How to better track customer-exposed regressions in presence of model distribution drift? (need ideas from research/applied-ml)
- Do we want a shared canary infrastructure offering in Dedicated that supports live splits by customer-id? (platform-engineering input required)

Immediate next steps (owner = Aisha):
- Get initial feedback from Jin and Miguel by EOD 2026-10-05 on threshold numbers and canary cadence.
- Draft a one-click Jira template for the standard sprint by 2026-10-12 and post to Confluence.
- Run trial with one upcoming feature change (ENG-7438) and capture lessons.

Notes to self / scratchpad (informal):
- Consider defaulting canary to region-limited first (us-west) to reduce blast radius.
- Want a small automated tool that creates the watch dashboard when you create the ticket (low priority).
- Keep language concise so product teams actually use this.

Referenced docs / helpful links (to paste into ticket):
- Confluence: SLO design patterns (link above)
- Internal runbook template: /confluence/ops/runbooks/service-cutover-template
- Example canary dashboard: dashboards/canary-ps-templates

-- end of playbook (working doc).

Revision history:
- 2026-09-15 Aisha: initial draft
- 2026-09-29 Miguel: added canary decision matrix and rollback triggers
- 2026-10-02 Jin: clarified fast-track flow and added acceptance criteria
